Bloomberg reports that Apple is targeting an OLED-equipped iPad mini launch before October this year, and has revealed the expected update timeline for the entry-level iPad, iPad Air, and iPad Pro. Details below.

「Half a century's biggest iPad mini overhaul」

Although rumours of an OLED display on the next iPad mini have been circulating for some time, Bloomberg has now provided a more precise launch window.

According to the latest report, "Apple is preparing to release a new OLED iPad mini (internal codename J510) as early as this autumn, with sales planned to begin in October." The report also notes that Apple "is developing an OLED upgrade for the iPad Air," but "has no current plans to equip the entry-level iPad with OLED, and will continue to use the cheaper LCD screen in the near term."

Earlier this week, Weibo tipster yeux1122 also said the iPad mini would adopt an OLED display, but claimed the device would not feature ProMotion technology, with the refresh rate remaining at a fixed 60Hz.

Returning to the Bloomberg report, it points out that adding OLED technology could push the iPad mini's price even higher. The current starting price of the device is US$599, already an increase from the US$499 it was priced at before Apple raised prices across most of its product lines a few weeks ago.

The report also shared Apple's expected timeline for the rest of the iPad lineup:

According to sources familiar with the matter, the new entry-level iPad with internal codename J581 is expected to launch as early as the first quarter of next year. The main change will be a processor upgrade rather than a major external design overhaul. The new iPad Air will continue to be available in 11-inch and 13-inch sizes. New versions with internal codenames J807 and J837 are expected to be released in spring. Apple also plans to launch a new iPad Pro in the same period, which Bloomberg previously reported on last month.

Finally, Bloomberg reaffirmed an earlier report from a few days ago, saying Apple is expected to update the Apple Pencil next year, with the new model possibly adopting a swappable battery design.
